clue.text: Discontented movement when a barbarian chief holds a bearer of disease

indicators.note: the barbarian chief is said to hold the disease carrier, so it goes inside them

parts.note: the Huns were the barbarian invaders of the late Roman empire
arch- as a word means chief or principal, as in arch-enemy
a germ is a microbe that carries illness

explanation.surface: A tribal leader carrying an infection leads a disgruntled march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chief' looks like it qualifies 'barbarian', but it is a separate piece: the disease carrier is held between the barbarian and the chief.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunger march is a protest procession by the unemployed or poor, a movement of the discontented.

clue.text: Give us time for practice

parts.note: taken as written
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone asks for time to rehearse.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is customary practice, the habitual way something is done.

clue.text: A collector is one who is inclined to gravity

indicators.note: to here means added on, with the gravity symbol placed alongside the inclined one

parts.note: g is the physics symbol for acceleration due to gravity
someone who leans or tilts is a leaner

explanation.surface: A collector is described as someone with a serious bent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gravity' looks like seriousness, but it is the physics symbol G.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleaner gathers up leftover grain or scraps of information, so is a collector.

clue.text: Rough but provided with some comfort underfoot

definitions.meaning: read as ..., furnished with a rug on the floor

explanation.definitionFit: Rugged terrain is rough; read as a made-up participle it means having had floor coverings laid.

clue.text: Plant in a vessel like this

parts.note: a can is a container or vessel
thus means in this way or like this

explanation.surface: A plant is shown sitting in a pot in a certain way.
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthus is a Mediterranean plant with spiny leaves, the model for Corinthian column decoration.

clue.text: Clothes arrive including something for fixing the collar unfinished

indicators.note: the arriving word takes in the shortened collar fastener

parts.note: to come is to arrive

indicators.note: the collar fastener loses its final letter, so it is left incomplete

parts.note: a collar stud fastens a detachable collar to a shirt

explanation.surface: Garments turn up with the collar fastening not quite done.
explanation.walkthrough: A collar stud fixes a detachable collar to an old-style shirt; 'unfinished' drops its last letter, D.
explanation.definitionFit: A costume is a set of clothes, especially an outfit for a role or period.

clue.text: Make E V Morgan wrongly exchange about a thousand for muddy land with trees

indicators.note: the letters of the named person are set down wrongly, that is in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the exchange word is placed around the symbol for a thousand

parts.note: to swap is to exchange
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone called E V Morgan is told to trade something for boggy woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' is a link; 'wrongly' rearranges the initials and surname into the tree word, and 'exchange about a thousand' builds the boggy word.
explanation.definitionFit: A mangrove swamp is a tidal marsh thick with salt-tolerant trees growing in mud.

clue.text: Object when a politician is given a note in money

indicators.note: the politician and note are placed inside the money word

parts.note: coin is money in metal form
MP is a Member of Parliament
la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone protests when an MP receives cash and a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: To object is to protest or grumble, the verb sense here.

clue.text: Keen competitions require the French marriage partners

parts.note: to need is to require
le is French for the
matches are pairings, as when people are a good match in marriage

explanation.surface: Fierce contests demand French spouses.
explanation.definitionFit: A needle match is a fiercely contested game, often with personal rivalry.

clue.text: Knowing it would be pointless if there were fighting

parts.note: if there were fighting, there would be a war on
pointless says the answer, with its compass point E taken off, would leave only the fighting phrase, so that point is the extra letter

explanation.surface: Being knowing would be useless in a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is the answer: take E (a compass point, hence 'pointless') off it and A WAR is left. 'Knowing' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being conscious or informed of something is the same as knowing it.

clue.text: Pleased to pelt a politician

parts.note: glad means pleased
to stone someone is to pelt them with rocks

explanation.surface: A crowd is happy to throw things at an MP.
explanation.definitionFit: William Ewart Gladstone was a four-time Liberal Prime Minister of Victorian Britain.

clue.text: Be right and gentle about place, for it should not be built on

definitions.text: place, for it should not be built on

indicators.note: about here means around in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to be correct and kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges BE, R and GENTLE together; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A green belt is protected countryside round a town where building is restricted.

clue.text: Raised with a degree course at heart

clue.text: Belonging to us holding a party when there is evidence of cooking

indicators.note: the possessive word holds the party word within it

parts.note: ours means belonging to us
a do is a party or social event

explanation.surface: We host a party where kitchen smells give the game away.
explanation.definitionFit: Smells drifting from a kitchen are the evidence that food is being cooked.

clue.text: A bit of music for a public individual

parts.note: overt means open or public
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A short tune is offered for a well-known person.
explanation.definitionFit: An overtone is a higher harmonic sounding above a fundamental note, a small element of musical sound.

clue.text: Part of plane which is in time after fuels have been changed

indicators.note: after places the time word following the rearranged letters
the fuels word has been altered, its letters put in a new order

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Something on an aircraft is in order once the fuel types have been swapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have been changed' turns FUELS into FUSEL; 'which is in' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuselage is the main body of an aircraft.

clue.text: They act unfairly and sound like animals

indicators.note: sound like says the word for the animals is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: cheetahs are big cats, the fastest land animals

explanation.surface: Some cheats resemble beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: People who cheat break rules to gain an unfair advantage.

clue.text: Agreement among the crew makes sense

indicators.note: the agreement word sits among the letters of the crew

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen
yes expresses agreement

explanation.surface: Consensus within a team makes sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the crew' is a rowing eight; 'makes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight is one of the five senses, the power of seeing.

clue.text: Repeat within the hearing of the waiter at every opportunity

indicators.note: within says the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Say it again in earshot of the waiter at every chance.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run through waITER AT Every; 'the hearing of' is surface dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to say or do again, to repeat.

clue.text: The bachelor is without a tear for a girl

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the bachelor goes round the tear

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts
to rend is to tear

explanation.surface: An unmarried man has no rip in his clothes, all for a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it has its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Brenda is a girl's name.

clue.text: When a girl follows sport it is a disease

indicators.note: follows places the girl after the sport

parts.note: RU is rugby union
Bella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl takes up a game and falls ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubella, or German measles, is a contagious viral illness.

clue.text: One who gives money is about right for begging

indicators.note: the giver of money is around the abbreviation for right

parts.note: a payer hands over money

explanation.surface: A donor hovers about something right for the needy.
explanation.definitionFit: A prayer is an earnest request, so it is a form of begging or entreaty.

clue.text: If red this twig is dried up

indicators.note: If here frames a condition: with the letter added the answer becomes the longer word, so the answer is that word less it

parts.note: to wither is to dry up and shrivel
R is a common abbreviation for red

explanation.surface: A twig that has gone red seems shrivelled.
explanation.walkthrough: Add R (red) to the answer ('this') and you get WITHER, dried up.
explanation.definitionFit: A withe is a pliant twig, such as willow, used for binding.

clue.text: Agile as one who has to loot an article during a performance

indicators.note: the looting and the article happen during the performance, so they go inside it

parts.note: an act is a stage performance
to rob is to loot
a is the indefinite article
the suffix -ic makes an adjective meaning of or like, as in being like the person just described

explanation.surface: Nimble, like a thief who must strike an object mid-show.
explanation.walkthrough: The performer who robs during an act is an ACROBAT pun; 'as' adds the -IC ending that turns the noun into an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrobats are famously nimble, so the related adjective means agile.

clue.text: Area for publication

definitions.meaning: an expanse of land or region
a short printed pamphlet, often religious or political

explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a stretch of land, and also a pamphlet issued to argue a cause.

clue.text: Routinely has union backing and confused city

indicators.note: backing means the union's letters go in reverse order

parts.note: NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers

indicators.note: the word and is confused, its letters jumbled

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A trade union, in muddle, routinely supports a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns NUM into MUN; 'confused' makes DAN from AND. ELY is an English cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in an ordinary, everyday, humdrum way is doing it routinely.

clue.text: Permission to depart

definitions.meaning: to go away from a place

explanation.definitionFit: Leave is consent, as when soldiers get time off; to leave is to go away.

clue.text: Vets manners in the style of Jeeves and company

indicators.note: in the style of loosely signals that the letters are refashioned into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone checks the etiquette of a fictional valet and friends.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeeves is P G Wodehouse's fictional valet, the model domestic manservant.
explanation.definitionFit: Butlers and valets are male domestic staff, of whom Jeeves is the archetype.
